title: Eggs Benedict
subtitle: Poached eggs and ham on muffins with hollandaise
excerpt: Toasted English muffins topped with grilled ham, perfectly poached eggs, and a rich, emulsified hollandaise sauce. The classic American brunch dish, well worth the effort.

recipe.sourceNotes: Eggs Benedict is a brunch classic that is claimed by several New York restaurants and individuals, with the most widely cited origin story placing it at Delmonico's restaurant in Manhattan in the 1860s, where a regular customer named Lemuel Benedict supposedly requested the dish. The defining components are an English muffin, grilled ham (traditionally Canadian back bacon), a poached egg, and hollandaise sauce. The difficulty of the dish lies in making hollandaise successfully and holding it at temperature while poaching the eggs, and poaching the eggs perfectly while the hollandaise is ready. Hollandaise is an emulsified butter sauce using egg yolk and clarified or whole butter: it is one of the five French mother sauces. It must be served warm, not hot (high heat breaks the emulsion) and is made to order rather than reheated.

recipeTools.notes: A saucepan for poaching the eggs and a small saucepan for the hollandaise. A heatproof bowl for the hollandaise.

content.text: Make the hollandaise first and keep it warm in the bowl set over barely warm water. Poach the eggs last: they need only 3 minutes and will be the freshest element. Use the freshest eggs available for poaching: fresh egg whites hold together around the yolk; older whites spread and produce ragged-looking poached eggs. The water for poaching should be just below a simmer with a splash of white wine vinegar: the gentle heat and the acid help the white set quickly around the yolk. Slide each egg into the water from a cup rather than cracking directly in.

items.preparation: thick-cut; split and toasted, or use English muffins if available
1 tbsp for hollandaise, 1 tbsp for poaching

content.text: Make the hollandaise: melt the butter in a small saucepan. Whisk the 4 egg yolks and the white wine vinegar together in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water. Whisk for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture is thick and pale and leaves a trail. Remove from the heat and whisk in the melted butter a few drops at a time, then in a thin stream. Season with lemon juice, cayenne, and salt. Keep warm over the warm water.

Grill or pan-fry the ham until hot. Toast and butter the muffins. Fill a wide saucepan with water 6 cm deep and bring to a bare simmer. Add the white wine vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup, then tip gently into the water. Poach for 3 minutes until the white is set and the yolk is still runny. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain.

Assemble: place the toasted muffin halves on warm plates. Top each with a slice of ham and a poached egg. Spoon hollandaise generously over the top. Season with a little black pepper and serve immediately.
